Why: Bathroom 1: the saved rectangle lies beside the WC, inside the room, clear of solid fixtures

Why: Bathroom 1: door overlap 0.2367 m; under-basin overlap 0 m. The saved circle meets both

Requirement: One living room or bedroom: (area ≥ 9 m² AND height ≥ 2.2 m) OR volume ≥ 20 m³.
Why: Main-room candidate: 42.75 m², height 2.5 m, volume 106.87 m³. The area-and-height
Requirement: Estimated habitable area ≥ 28 m² for 2 occupants.
Why: Estimated habitable area: 99.93 m²; meets the 28 m² requirement.
Requirement: Estimated habitable volume ≥ 66 m³ for 2 occupants.
Why: Estimated habitable volume: 249.82 m³; meets the 66 m³ requirement.
Requirement: Each kitchen: declared normal extraction ≥ 105 m³/h for 3 main rooms.
Why: 3 main rooms; 1 kitchen(s). Declared normal flow per kitchen: 105 m³/h; meets the 105
m³/h minimum. Airflow is a fixed scenario input, not a model prediction.
Requirement: Each bathroom: declared normal extraction ≥ 30 m³/h for 3 main rooms.
Why: 3 main rooms; 1 bathroom(s). Declared normal flow per bathroom: 30 m³/h; meets the 30
m³/h minimum. Airflow is a fixed scenario input, not a model prediction.
Requirement: Occupant-adjustable reduced mode: total extraction ≥ 75 m³/h AND each kitchen ≥ 45 m³/h.
Why: 3 main rooms. Declared reduced total: 75 m³/h (meets 75); per-kitchen flow: 45 m³/h
(meets 45). Both requirements must pass; these flows are scenario inputs.
Room types are the model's saved semantic labels. Metric dimensions use the declared scale; other furniture and door swings are unobserved.
Bathroom objects are hypothetical scenario placements, not GSDiff predictions. The inset shows one shared proposal for C036/C037/C041; it does not establish a route through the dwelling.
Supporting definitions: C034, C079, C080. These supply parameters; they are not scored checks.
